sourceStrategy.principle: Do not treat the REVISATHON compilation as the sole content authority. Clearly label source-derived facts, cross-source synthesis, and unresolved discrepancies.

aspirantCoverageQuestions: Can I define the construct precisely and distinguish it from its nearest confusable construct?
Can I explain the mechanism, stages, assumptions, dimensions or classification without looking?
Can I identify the theorist/researcher, theory, key term, study or instrument where the syllabus/source expects it?
Can I apply it to a short scenario and identify why plausible distractors are wrong?
Can I interpret the relevant diagram, sequence, formula, table, score or result where applicable?
Can I distinguish competing theories, tests, designs, scales, therapies or models?
Can I answer the kinds of matching, chronology, statement-combination, assertion/reason, calculation and application questions actually evidenced in the PYQs?
Is the chunk appropriately sized to learn and retrieve in one sitting, or does it contain multiple independent objectives?
sourceUseRules: Official syllabus defines coverage and all 10 existing units stay unchanged.
Use at least one suitable conceptual source plus PYQ evidence for priority content; add a topic-specific source when available.
Use textbooks for explanation and conceptual boundaries; use PYQs to determine what must be discriminated, applied or retrieved, not as the only source of truth.
Record file name and page/chapter/section for claims that will appear in learner-facing content.
Do not infer answer keys, exam years, or missing question options from headings or coaching commentary.
When sources disagree, record the disagreement and resolve it against syllabus context and stronger primary/reference evidence; do not silently blend contradictions.
Use Kaplan/AP material only for transferable concepts within syllabus scope, never to expand the NET syllabus by default.
Keep authentic PYQs separate from newly written MCQs and label generated practice honestly.
